DOCUMENTED: Bolton station 2, "a native village-site at the Kalch Hoek, a hill which overlooked the Collect ponds ... probably situated on the line of Elm street [Lafayette St], between Duane and Worth streets, the center being cut by the line of Pearl street, which, when graded, disclosed masses of shells"; Parker (New York Co. no. 9) "village site ... overlooking a small lake near Canal street ... called Shell Point". Stokes puts the locality Werpoes north of the pond (a 1638 grant "near Werpoes" at Grand and Mulberry Sts). ESTIMATE: count, spread; end = the Manhattan purchase of 1626 (no record of when the village was left).

name: Rechtauck / Nechtanc, Corlears Hook
shape_note: Bark- or mat-covered wigwams on bent-sapling frames, drawn 5 m across (early_nyc.md s.3). DOCUMENTED: Bolton station 3, "a village-site on Corlears hook ... The most natural position for such a station was near a fresh-water pond and brook at the present Jefferson, Henry, Clinton, and Madison streets"; Van Corlaer leased his plantation "with the contiguous Hook, called, in the Indian language, Nechtanc" in 1640 (Stokes). End: people who had taken refuge here were killed by Dutch soldiers on 25 Feb 1643 (Kieft's War). ESTIMATE: count, spread; the position is Bolton's inference, not a find. Point moved 80 m to the nearest dry ground of the 1609 layer (the source's spot is water, marsh or pond there, or water today).

name: Longhouse of the Najack people seen by Danckaerts, 1679
shape_note: ONE LONGHOUSE, MEASURED BY AN EYEWITNESS: Jasper Danckaerts, 30 Sept 1679, at "the plantation of the Najack Indians, which was planted with maize ... seven or eight families, and twenty or twenty-two persons ... Their house was low and long, about sixty feet long and fourteen or fifteen feet wide [18.3 x 4.4 m]. The bottom was earth, the sides and roof were made of reed and the bark of chestnut trees; the posts ... limbs of trees stuck in the ground ... The top, or ridge of the roof was open about half a foot wide, from one end to the other ... doors, which were at both ends". They lived on "a small corner" of Jacques Cortelyou's land for twenty bushels of maize a year. start_year 1652 = the sale of Nayack, after which they stayed as tenants. name: Schenck house on Mill Island

name: Oude Dorp
shape_note: Village houses; SIZE ESTIMATE (8 x 6 m, one storey and garret, after the Achtervelt house of 1638). COUNT FROM AN EYEWITNESS: Danckaerts, Oct 1679, past the rocky point at the Narrows "a pretty little sand bay, and a small creek, and not far from there, cattle and houses ... the houses which constituted the Oude Dorp ... There were seven houses, but only three in which any body lived. The others were abandoned ... because the ground around this village was worn out". Founded August 1661 under Pierre Billiou (Wikipedia). ESTIMATE: position (near South Beach, good to about 500 m), end 1700.
